model.name: Message
model.purpose: Govern communications between agents as exchangeable message records with parts and attachments, conversation grouping, channel endpoints, delivery and disposition evidence, and contact consent, independent of any one transport or storage format.
model.scope_statement: This aggregate covers the semantics of sending, carrying, delivering, reading, failing, recalling or deleting, and retaining a unit of communication from an originator to one or more recipients, including the envelope/content split, multipart bodies, threading, addresses, hop handoff, delivery status, post-delivery disposition, and permission to contact. It is channel-neutral: email, federated social notes, clinical communication records, chat, postal and broadcast share the same exchange, transport-evidence and custody concerns even when their on-the-wire encodings differ.
in_scope: A message as a unit of communication with origin identifiers, originator and recipient roles, origination time, subject or summary, and sensitivity or category.
Multipart content entities, media types, transfer encodings, inline parts and references to carried documents.
Conversation grouping via reply identifiers, references, threads, topics and participation.
Transport channels, providers, address schemes and reachable endpoints, including group, list, public and blind-copy audiences.
Envelope routing, responsibility handoff, relays, gateways, mailing-list expansion and alias expansion.
Delivery status evidence distinct from content, including failure, delay, success, relay into a foreign system and expansion.
Post-delivery disposition evidence, including display, deletion, processing, dispatch, retraction, tombstones and refused receipts.
Consent, preference, objection and block records that authorize or forbid contact on a channel for a purpose.
Copy ownership, access scopes, archival retention, legal hold, erasure and provenance of communication records.
out_of_scope: Person, organization, device or agent identity masters; this model only references those actors as senders, recipients, providers or consent subjects.
The governed document or media object itself when a message merely points at it as an attachment or payload reference.
Identifier scheme registries and language/terminology systems; this model consumes scheme and language tags.
Packet, session or broker protocols as such (TCP, SMTP command sequences, MQTT topics, AMQP frames) except as a channel type and envelope fields they expose.
Real-time media sessions, presence, typing indicators and other ephemeral session state that is not a retained message record.
General-purpose consent, privacy notices or marketing preference centres beyond permission to be contacted.
Cryptographic key management, though signatures, hashes and authentication results may be recorded as evidence.
Social graph membership except where a followers or public collection is used as an addressing target.

boundary_notes.distinction: A message may carry or point to documents; the document model owns content persistence, versioning and format of those artifacts. This model owns only the pointer, filename, media type, checksum and the fact that they were conveyed.

Authors, senders, recipients, reporting agents and consent subjects are references to actor masters. Mailbox strings, actor IRIs and display names live here as addressing and originator fields, not as identity records.
addr-spec, actor IRI, telephone and postal schemes are registered identifier schemes. This model records the scheme, the address value and verification state, not the scheme registry.
Natural-language tagging of subject, body and Activity Streams nameMap/contentMap values is alignment to a language system; this model stores the tags and maps, not the language catalogue.

FHIR Communication is a clinical or business record that information was shared, including failed attempts. Encounter duration, Composition sections and AuditEvent system-to-system disclosure logs are neighboring records, not this aggregate.

ActivityPub Create wraps a Note or other object for federation. This model treats the Create/Note pair as one communication unit plus delivery targeting; likes, follows and profile objects remain in the social-activity neighbor except when they are themselves the message.

sources.title: RFC 5322 Internet Message Format
sources.relevance: Normative Internet Message Format: header fields, originator and destination semantics, Message-ID, In-Reply-To, References, Date, trace and resent fields. Companion to RFC 5321 envelope. Updated by RFC 6854.

sources.title: RFC 5321 Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
sources.relevance: Normative mail object split into envelope and content; MAIL FROM and RCPT TO; client/server MTA roles; responsibility handoff after successful DATA; relay, gateway, alias and mailing-list behaviour.

sources.title: RFC 2045 MIME Part One: Format of Internet Message Bodies
sources.relevance: Normative MIME entity, body part, Content-Type, Content-Transfer-Encoding, Content-ID and Content-Description. Composite multipart and message types are specified with RFC 2046.

sources.title: RFC 3464 An Extensible Message Format for Delivery Status Notifications
sources.relevance: Normative DSN: per-message and per-recipient fields, action values failed/delayed/delivered/relayed/expanded, status codes, Original-Envelope-Id distinct from Message-ID, gatewaying of foreign notifications.

sources.title: RFC 8098 Message Disposition Notification
sources.relevance: Internet Standard (STD 85) for post-delivery MDNs: Disposition-Notification-To request, disposition types displayed/deleted/dispatched/processed, manual versus automatic modes, privacy constraints, no MDN of an MDN.

sources.title: Activity Streams 2.0
sources.relevance: Normative social object model: id IRI, attributedTo, to/bto/cc/bcc/audience, inReplyTo, published/updated, attachment, mediaType, natural-language maps, RFC 3339 timestamps, collections.

sources.title: ActivityPub
sources.relevance: Normative federation: actor inbox and outbox, addressing and delivery, Create wrapping, Update, Delete/Tombstone, Undo, Block, sharedInbox, transient objects without id, inbox forwarding for ghost replies.

sources.title: Activity Vocabulary
sources.relevance: Normative activity and object types used as messages or wrappers: Create, Delete, Update, Undo, Read, View, Block, Note, Tombstone and addressing properties.

sources.title: FHIR Resource Communication R5
sources.relevance: Clinical or business record of information being transmitted, including planned and failed attempts. Status, medium, sent/received, payload, inResponseTo, sender, recipient. Distinct from AuditEvent and Encounter.

sources.title: Art. 7 GDPR Conditions for consent
sources.relevance: Live retrieval of GDPR Article 7 text: demonstrable consent, distinguishable request, withdrawal as easy as grant, withdrawal does not undo prior lawful processing. Authentic instrument is CELEX:32016R0679. Secondary presenter is gdpr-info.eu.

layers.name: Message unit and origin
layers.description: The atomic communication object, its identifiers, originator roles, origination time and classification.

findings.name: Origin and local message identity
findings.description: A message MUST be correlatable across copies, reports and replies. RFC 5322 Message-ID SHOULD be present and identifies content; RFC 3464 Original-Envelope-Id identifies the submission transaction and is not the Message-ID. ActivityPub objects distributed on the social web MUST have unique global identifiers unless intentionally transient. FHIR Communication carries business identifiers that remain constant as the resource is updated. A date is not an identifier. Local store keys are subordinate to the origin identifier.

questions.text: What is the authoritative origin identifier of this message, which system issued it, and under which scheme?
answer_data: Structured record: origin-message-id, origin-id-scheme, issuing-system-ref, issued-at RFC 3339.

questions.text: Is there a submission or envelope transaction identifier distinct from the content identifier, and must it be preserved for delivery reports?
answer_data: Optional string envelope-transaction-id with case-preservation flag and correlation-to-dsn boolean.

questions.text: Is this communication intentionally transient, and if so may a global identifier be omitted?
answer_data: Boolean is-transient plus expected-lifetime duration or expiry RFC 3339.

questions.text: What local store key does this Dimension assign, and how does it reference the origin identifier?
answer_data: local-store-id plus origin-message-id foreign key; never a date used as id.

findings.name: Originator roles and message lifecycle
findings.description: RFC 5322 distinguishes author (From), transmitter (Sender, required when From has multiple mailboxes), and suggested reply addresses (Reply-To). Date is the time the creator marked the message complete, not the time of transport. FHIR Communication.status is a required modifier: preparation, in-progress, not-done, on-hold, stopped, completed, entered-in-error, unknown. ActivityPub Create, Update, Delete and Undo are the corresponding social lifecycle verbs. Origination Date and FHIR sent/received are event times; ingestion into a store is a separate observation time.

questions.text: When was the message completed, when was it sent, and when was this copy ingested, each as RFC 3339 with offset or Z?

layers.name: Body parts and attachments
layers.description: Structured content entities, media types, encodings, language, and pointers to carried documents.

findings.name: MIME entities and payload parts
findings.description: A MIME entity is the headers plus body of a message or of a body part. Content-Type gives type/subtype and parameters such as charset and boundary. Content-Transfer-Encoding is 7bit, 8bit, binary, quoted-printable or base64. Content-ID labels a part; Content-Description is human description. Nested encodings of composite types are forbidden. Activity Streams objects carry content/contentMap, mediaType and attachment. FHIR Communication.payload may be attachment, reference or codeable concept. Default without Content-Type is text/plain; charset=us-ascii.

answer_data: List of parts: part-index, parent-part-ref, media-type, transfer-encoding, byte-size, content-id.

answer_data: language-tag and optional content-map/name-map/summary-map with BCP 47 keys.

findings.name: Attachment and payload references
findings.description: Attachments are pointers from a message to carried or referenced documents, not the document master. MIME uses Content-Disposition filename and Content-ID for cid: references. Activity Streams attachment is a qualified link with mediaType. FHIR payload may be a contentReference to another resource. Integrity of the pointer is a checksum on the conveyed octets, not document-model versioning.

layers.name: Thread, reply and audience
layers.description: Conversation grouping, reply chains, participants and public versus blind addressing.

findings.name: Reply correlation and conversation grouping
findings.description: RFC 5322 In-Reply-To and References identify parent and ancestor Message-IDs; they SHOULD appear in replies. Activity Streams inReplyTo and replies collection, and FHIR inResponseTo, are the corresponding links. A thread is a derived grouping, not an on-the-wire required object. ActivityPub inbox forwarding exists so that replies addressed to a collection the origin cannot deliver to still reach participants (ghost-reply problem). Resent fields reintroduce a message into transport and are not the same as a reply.

answer_data: in-reply-to-ids, references-ids, resolution-status per id.

questions.text: What thread identifier and topic group this message, and when did the thread start?
answer_data: thread-id, topic, started-at, participant-count.

questions.text: Is this a reply, a resend/reintroduction, a forward, or an in-response-to clinical follow-up?
answer_data: relation-kind enum reply | resent | forward | in-response-to | new-root, plus evidence fields.

questions.text: Must this server forward the activity to collections it owns because the origin could not expand them?
answer_data: Boolean forward-inbox-required, owned-collection-refs, first-seen-activity-id.

findings.name: Audience, copies and participation
findings.description: RFC 5322 To is primary recipients, Cc others who should receive, Bcc recipients not revealed to others; Bcc may be stripped or only shown to Bcc recipients. Group syntax can name a set without listing mailboxes. Activity Streams to, bto, cc, bcc and audience, plus the Public collection, are the social equivalents; bto/bcc MUST be removed before federated delivery but still used to compute recipients. ActivityPub delivery expands collections, de-duplicates, and MUST NOT deliver an actor their own activity. FHIR has sender and recipient. Blind-copy confidentiality conflicts with some delivery reports that reveal Final-Recipient.

layers.name: Channel and address
layers.description: Transport medium, provider and reachable endpoints of agents.

findings.name: Channel type and provider
findings.description: A channel is the transport medium used or intended, not the message. RFC 5321 defines SMTP client, server, relay, gateway, originating and delivery systems. ActivityPub uses inbox and outbox OrderedCollections and optional sharedInbox. FHIR Communication.medium records how the communication was conveyed. Gatewaying may transform headers and envelopes in ways forbidden to a pure relay. Channel type is classification here; credentials and live sockets are out of scope.

answer_data: channel-type, provider-ref, hop-role enum origin | relay | gateway | delivery, protocol-profile.

answer_data: outbox-iri, inbox-iri, shared-inbox-iri, posted-at.

questions.text: If a clinical communication, what medium codes describe how information was shared?
answer_data: List of FHIR medium CodeableConcepts with system and code.

findings.name: Addressable endpoints
findings.description: An address is a reachable endpoint of an agent on a channel. RFC 5321 mailbox is local-part@domain; local-part is case-sensitive and interpreted only by the domain host; FQDNs are required on the public Internet except postmaster. RFC 5322 mailbox may include a display name or a group. ActivityPub actors are dereferenceable IRIs with inbox. Verification of an address is a custody fact, not the address value itself. Identifier scheme registration belongs to the naming sibling.

layers.name: Envelope, handoff and delivery status
layers.description: Transport envelope, hop responsibility, traces, and machine-readable delivery outcomes.

findings.name: Envelope versus content and responsibility handoff
findings.description: SMTP transports a mail object with envelope (originator reverse-path, recipient forward-paths, optional extension material) and content (header section plus body). After the server issues a success response at end of mail data, it MUST accept responsibility to deliver or report failure. Relays add trace Received lines and MUST NOT otherwise modify message data; gateways MAY transform. Null reverse-path MAIL FROM:<> is used for DSNs and MDNs to prevent loops. ActivityPub delivery POSTs an activity to target inboxes after expanding to/bto/cc/bcc/audience.

findings.name: Delivery status evidence
findings.description: A DSN reports per-recipient action failed, delayed, delivered, relayed or expanded, plus a transport-independent status code. Delivered includes delivery to a mailing-list exploder and does not mean the message was read. Expanded is used for multi-recipient aliases and is not terminal. Relayed means gatewaying into an environment that will not emit success DSNs. Original-Recipient versus Final-Recipient capture rewriting. Reporting-MTA, Remote-MTA, Arrival-Date, Last-Attempt-Date and Will-Retry-Until support delay and operations. FHIR status not-done with statusReason records failed clinical communications. DSN forgery and confidentiality of forwarding addresses are first-class risks.

layers.name: Disposition, read and recall
layers.description: Post-delivery user-agent disposition, privacy-preserving receipts, and retraction or deletion.

findings.name: Read receipts and disposition notifications
findings.description: MDNs report post-delivery disposition: displayed, deleted, dispatched or processed, with action mode manual-action or automatic-action and sending mode MDN-sent-manually or MDN-sent-automatically. Displayed does not guarantee the content was read or understood. Recipients MAY silently ignore MDN requests. Default is not to send MDNs; user consent is strongly recommended. An MDN MUST NOT be sent automatically if Disposition-Notification-To differs from Return-Path. An MDN MUST NOT have a Disposition-Notification-To field. Activity Vocabulary Read and View are related social types. FHIR completed is not an MDN.

findings.name: Recall, update, delete and tombstone
findings.description: Internet Mail has no interoperable recall standard; retraction is channel-specific. ActivityPub Update applies partial updates client-to-server and full representation server-to-server. Delete MAY replace the object with a Tombstone and SHOULD yield HTTP 410 with Tombstone or 404. Undo reverses Like, Follow or Block but Create is inverted by Delete, not Undo. FHIR stopped, not-done and entered-in-error cover cancelled or erroneous clinical communications. Block SHOULD prevent the blocked actor interacting and SHOULD NOT be delivered to the blocked actor.

layers.name: Consent, preference and objection
layers.description: Lawful permission, withdrawal, channel preferences and blocks for contact.

findings.name: Consent to be contacted
findings.description: Where processing is based on consent, the controller must be able to demonstrate it. Consent in a written declaration that also concerns other matters must be clearly distinguishable. The data subject may withdraw at any time; withdrawal is as easy as grant and does not undo prior lawful processing. MDN sending likewise requires user consent and defaults to not sending. ActivityPub Block is a hard preference against interaction. This finding is contact-specific consent, not general-purpose privacy notices. Unsolicited-communication statutes such as CAN-SPAM, PECR and TCPA are alignments with regional gaps.

layers.name: Copy ownership and access
layers.description: Who owns which copy, who may read it, and which internals are omitted from which views.

findings.name: Sender record versus recipient copies
findings.description: The sender owns the origin message record; each recipient owns their received copy. Bcc and bto identities present on one copy MUST NOT leak through another copy or through a DSN that the site chooses to omit for confidentiality. ActivityPub outbox contents are filtered by the requestor's permission; unauthenticated reads see only Public posts. Inbox owners can typically read all of their inbox. AS2 privacy considerations require documenting collection of sensitive personal information and defaulting to opt-in for extra detail. Archive access is a distinct authorized view.

layers.name: Retention, erasure and provenance
layers.description: How long communication records are kept, when they are erased, and what evidence supports integrity.

findings.name: Retention, legal hold and erasure
findings.description: Communication records are personal data when they identify natural persons. GDPR Article 7 withdrawal does not by itself erase historical messages that were lawfully sent. Erasure, restriction and objection rights (Articles 17 and 21) interact with legal holds, medical record retention and provider logs. ActivityPub Delete/Tombstone is origin-side deletion and does not guarantee every federated copy vanishes. DSN and MDN evidence may need a different retention than message bodies. ISO 15489-style records controls are an alignment gap unless adopted by the Dimension.

findings.name: Provenance, integrity and authentication evidence
findings.description: RFC 5322/5321 Received traces document hops. DSN Reporting-MTA and MDN Reporting-UA identify reporters but are forgeable. ActivityPub servers SHOULD validate received content against origin and may use signatures; no single mechanism is mandated. ActivityPub source records markup provenance for later edits. AS2 documents can contain sensitive personal information and implementations MUST document collection and sharing. Checksums on parts, DKIM/SPF/DMARC authentication results and S/MIME signatures are relevant evidence; DKIM and S/MIME were not fetched as primary sources in this run and are marked as interoperability alignments with a gap.

composition.purpose: Individual authors, senders, recipients, reporting-UA users and consent subjects are person masters referenced, not duplicated.
Organizational originators, channel providers, reporting MTAs and clinical senders are organization masters.
Attachments and FHIR contentReference payloads resolve to governed documents; this model stores pointers, filenames and checksums only.
Address schemes (mailto, actor IRI, tel, postal) are registered identifier schemes consumed as address-scheme.
BCP 47 tags on parts and Activity Streams language maps are language-system values.
IMF header semantics are an alignment, not a claim that every channel serializes RFC 5322. Conflicts with RFC 3339 timestamps and IRI identifiers are recorded.
MIME entity, media type and transfer-encoding semantics align multipart content; RFC 2046 composite types are implied companions.
Actor-to-actor object and activity semantics, addressing properties and collections align social and chat-like channels.
Inbox/outbox delivery, Create wrapping, Delete/Tombstone, Block and inbox forwarding align federated delivery behaviour.
Clinical communication records, including failed attempts, status and payload, align health-industry use; they are not a substitute for transport payloads.
Article 7 conditions for consent align contact-permission records in the EEA; other jurisdictions need separate unsolicited-communication alignments.
DSN and MDN are aligned evidence formats; delivered is not displayed, and neither is a non-repudiation service.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension assigns local store keys and MUST bind each stored copy key to the origin identifier.
The adopting Dimension must resolve the referenced masters: person, organization, document record, identifier scheme and language system.
The adopting Dimension must declare retention classes, legal-hold authority and consent-evidence storage; ISO 15489-style records controls apply only where the Dimension adopts them.
The adopting Dimension must register the channel and provider records for each channel type it operates.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Registry entry vr.wm-rec-003 / WM-REC-003. Sibling world models are referenced under the world.* namespace (world.person, world.organization, world.document-record, world.identifier-naming, world.language-terminology); external alignments retain their standards-body namespaces (ietf.*, w3c.*, hl7.*, eu.*).

canonicalization_rules: Timestamps are stored as RFC 3339 date-times with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; RFC 5322 IMF Date is treated as an alignment, not identical syntax.
SMTP local-part case and exact spelling are preserved; rewriting is recorded as original-recipient versus final-recipient rather than applied silently.
Content hashes are computed over a declared canonicalization profile that is recorded with the digest.
patch_rules: Lifecycle, delivery and disposition fields are append-mostly: corrections are new evidence rows, not silent rewrites.
Content updates are permitted only where the channel supports Update and the actor owns the object; ActivityPub applies partial updates client-to-server and a full representation server-to-server.
Consent withdrawal is a timestamped update that sets withdrawn-at without deleting the grant evidence.
compatibility_rules: DSN delivered, MDN displayed and FHIR completed are not unified into one code; each keeps its own semantics.
Alignment to a standard is not a claim that a channel serializes that standard; claiming universal unsend or non-repudiation would be false conformance.
Origin identifier, envelope transaction identifier and local store key remain distinct layers and must not be merged.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier: RFC 5322 Message-ID, ActivityPub object id IRI, or FHIR Communication.identifier
A UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension
A date is not an identifier
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Event times (originated-at, sent-at, delivered-at, disposed-at) and observation or ingestion time are recorded separately as RFC 3339 date-times with seconds and an explicit offset or Z.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: No serial name is asserted by this model; ordered series such as trace hops and OrderedCollection positions are recorded by order plus event time, and the origin identifier remains the naming key for each artifact.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Origin identifiers are immutable after first successful send or publication. Each stored copy may have a distinct local key that MUST reference the origin identifier. Envelope-transaction-id, if present, is preserved for DSN correlation and MUST NOT be confused with Message-ID.

policies: Sender owns the origin message record; each recipient owns their received copy; consent subjects own their consent records.
Contact for a non-transactional purpose requires a recorded lawful basis or demonstrable consent; withdrawal is as easy as grant and is evaluated before send.
Bcc, bto and confidential forwarding addresses MUST NOT leak through other copies, public views or optional DSN fields.
MDNs and similar receipts are opt-in, at most one per recipient per user agent, and MUST NOT be generated for an MDN.
Relays accept responsibility to deliver or report failure; archives and legal holds override routine deletion but not the duty to record erasure requests.

read: Owner of a copy, an authorized delegate, or an archive reviewer under an audited compliance view.
Unauthenticated readers receive only Public or equivalent disclosed messages.
Thread summaries may omit bodies and other-recipient receipts.
create: Authenticated originator or client acting on an outbox MAY create a message, part set and send event.
MTAs and federated servers MAY create DSN, MDN or inbox items as side effects of delivery.
Consent subjects or controllers MAY create consent-grant records.
update: Originator MAY update content only where the channel supports Update and the actor owns the object.
Lifecycle, delivery and disposition fields are append-mostly; they are corrected with new evidence rows, not silent rewrites.
Consent MAY be withdrawn; withdrawal is an update that sets withdrawn-at without deleting the grant evidence.
delete: Originator MAY delete or tombstone where the channel supports it; federated copies may remain.
Erasure of personal data follows retention class and legal hold; refused erasure is recorded, not silently ignored.
Operational mailbox deletion does not delete compliance-archive or DSN evidence until those classes expire.

roles.name: originator-author
responsibilities: Compose content, set audience, request receipts only with awareness of privacy costs, and own the origin record.

roles.name: transmitting-sender
responsibilities: Submit the envelope, accept or transfer responsibility, and keep Sender distinct from From when they differ.

roles.name: recipient
responsibilities: Own the received copy, decide MDN emission, and exercise access, objection and erasure rights on that copy.

roles.name: channel-provider-mta
responsibilities: Relay or deliver, emit accurate DSNs, preserve traces, and not modify content except as a documented gateway.

roles.name: consent-subject
responsibilities: Grant, refuse or withdraw contact permission and block unwanted actors.

roles.name: archive-steward
responsibilities: Apply retention, holds and audited compliance views without exposing live channel credentials.

access.default_rule: Deny all reads except to the copy owner and processes acting for that owner; Public addressing is an explicit exception.
exceptions: Public or equivalent audience makes the message readable without authentication.
Authorized compliance-archive reviewers may read full bodies, delivery evidence and consent state under audit.
Bcc identities are visible only on copies that the Bcc policy allows.
Reporting-MTA operators may read DSN diagnostic fields required to repair delivery, omitting confidential forward paths when policy requires.
audit_requirements: Record who read a compliance-archive view, when, and under which mandate.
Record send, delivery-status, disposition, consent-grant, consent-withdraw, block, delete and erasure-request events with event time and ingestion time.
Do not treat DSN or MDN as non-repudiation; log that they are forgeable.

coverage.claim: This research defines a channel-neutral Message aggregate covering identity, content parts, threading, addressing, envelope handoff, DSN-class delivery evidence, MDN-class disposition, contact consent, copy ownership, retention and provenance, grounded in IETF RFC 5322/5321/2045/3464/8098, W3C Activity Streams 2.0, Activity Vocabulary and ActivityPub, HL7 FHIR Communication R5, and GDPR Article 7. It is not a claim of universal completeness across postal, SMS, Matrix, XMPP, JMAP or records-management standards that were not fetched as primary sources in this run.

checklist.notes: Origin Message-ID, ActivityPub object id, FHIR identifier, envelope-transaction-id and Dimension ULID are modelled with immutability and scheme.
Draft through sent, FHIR EventStatus including not-done and entered-in-error, Update/Delete/Tombstone/Undo, delayed DSN and expansion.
Author/sender/recipient, part-of, in-reply-to, attachment pointers, channel, address owner, DSN confirms, consent authorizes.
originated-at, sent-at, ingested-at, arrival, last-attempt, will-retry-until, disposed-at, granted-at, withdrawn-at as RFC 3339.
Trace hops, Reporting-MTA/UA, origin-fetch verification, hashes; DKIM/S/MIME noted as alignment gaps.
Sender origin record, recipient copies, consent-subject ownership, Bcc copy isolation.
Required From/Date in IMF, required FHIR status, DSN required fields, MDN Return-Path match, MIME encoding rules.
Default deny, Public exception, inbox/outbox permission filtering, compliance-archive exception, MDN privacy.
Retention classes, legal hold, GDPR withdrawal versus erasure, Tombstone versus purge, federated copy uncertainty.
Alignments to IMF, MIME, SMTP, DSN, MDN, AS2, ActivityPub, FHIR Communication and GDPR; conflicts recorded.
Article 7 demonstration, distinguishable request, easy withdrawal, MDN opt-in, Block.
DSN actions including delayed, relayed, expanded; FHIR not-done; delivered is not displayed.
Channel types, mailbox and actor IRI endpoints, group and Public collections, FQDN and local-part rules.
In-Reply-To, References, inReplyTo, inResponseTo, ghost-reply forwarding, resent versus reply.
Subject and FHIR category/priority are present; a dedicated sensitivity/classification code system was not taken from a primary information-security standard in this run.

known_omissions: Universal Postal Union addressing and physical delivery evidence were not fetched.
Matrix Client-Server event IDs, XMPP stanza IDs, JMAP, IMAP flags and RFC 8621 were not fetched as primary sources.
S/MIME, OpenPGP, DKIM, SPF and DMARC are relevant integrity evidence but were not primary-fetched; treated as alignment gaps.
ISO 15489 / MoReq records-management schedules are not primary-supported.
CAN-SPAM, ePrivacy/PECR and TCPA unsolicited-communication rules are region-specific and not fully sourced here.
RFC 4865 future-release, RFC 6530-6533 internationalized email, and RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe were not fetched.
SMS, RCS, mobile push and proprietary chat receipts lack a single primary mapping.
End-to-end encrypted envelopes (MLS, server-side fanout of ciphertext) are out of evidence for this run.
conflicts: RFC 5322 Date uses IMF date-time; Activity Streams requires RFC 3339 with optional omitted seconds. This model stores RFC 3339 and treats IMF Date as an alignment, not identical syntax.
SMTP envelope reverse-path need not equal header From; using header From as the responsible sender is a known error.
DSN action delivered is terminal and does not mean read; MDN displayed does not mean understood; FHIR completed is a clinical-record status. Do not unify these codes.
Message-ID identifies content; Original-Envelope-Id identifies submission; ActivityPub Create id and object id are distinct; local store keys are another layer.
ActivityPub Delete does not retract every federated copy; email has no standard recall. Claiming unsend would be a false conformance.
Bcc confidentiality versus DSN Final-Recipient and mailing-list MDN leakage are unresolved operational tensions; sites MAY omit fields.
GDPR erasure rights conflict with legal hold and medical-record retention; both must be representable without implying a single global outcome.
FHIR Communication is a record that sharing occurred, including failures, and is not the on-the-wire message object.
regional_assumptions: GDPR Article 7 is assumed for EEA-relevant contact consent; other regions may rely on contract, legitimate interest or sectoral anti-spam law instead.
SMTP FQDN and DNS MX routing assume Internet mail; isolated intranets and non-TCP transports are allowed by RFC 5321 but not detailed here.
ActivityPub HTTPS-dereferencable actor and object ids assume a web-origin server namespace.
FHIR Communication is typical of HL7-adopting health systems and is not a global clinical mandate.
Default MDN suppression reflects RFC 8098 privacy guidance, which some enterprise mail systems override by policy.
adversarial_checks: Could a forged DSN or MDN be treated as non-repudiation? No; RFC 3464 and RFC 8098 document forgery; evidence-grade remains unverified unless independently corroborated.

Could Bcc or confidential autoforward addresses leak via DSN Remote-MTA, Final-Recipient or propagated MDN requests? Yes; optional fields MUST be omissible and list exploders SHOULD NOT propagate MDN requests.
Could this model claim email recall because ActivityPub has Delete? No; recall-supported is per channel and defaults false for IMF/SMTP.
Could a date or sent-at be used as a message identifier? Forbidden by identity priority.
Could consent withdrawal be modelled as deleting the grant evidence? Forbidden; withdrawal is a timestamped event and prior lawful sends remain explicable.
Could FHIR AuditEvent replace Communication for clinician-to-clinician letters? No; HL7 distinguishes reviewable Communication in the patient record from system audit.
Could likes, follows or presence pings be stored as messages? Only if they are themselves the communication unit; otherwise they belong to social-activity or session neighbors.
